clips.send: Milledgeville. Secession — and a mock repeal. The secession convention met here in January 1861 and voted 208–89 to leave the Union. On November 23, 1864, Sherman’s left wing took the capital; Union officers held a mock session in the statehouse and “repealed” secession.

clips.send: Fort Pulaski. The blockade tightens. A brick fort guarding the mouth of the Savannah River, with brick walls about 7½ feet thick. Union rifled cannon on Tybee Island, 1 to 2 miles away, broke through the walls in about 30 hours. After it fell, Savannah was almost closed to blockade runners for the rest of the war.

clips.send: Fort McAllister. The door to the sea opens. An earthwork fort guarding the Ogeechee River south of Savannah. Union troops stormed it in about 15 minutes, opening contact with the Union navy and its supplies.

clips.send: Irwinville. The Confederate president is captured. After Richmond fell and Lee surrendered, Confederate President Jefferson Davis fled south. Union cavalry captured him at his camp near Irwinville, in south Georgia.

clips.send: Dalton and Resaca. The Atlanta Campaign begins. Sherman’s roughly 100,000 men faced Joseph E. Johnston’s roughly 60,000 near Dalton. Instead of attacking head-on, Sherman kept swinging around Johnston’s flank, forcing him to retreat south. Both armies followed the Western and Atlantic Railroad — the lifeline to Atlanta.

clips.send: Savannah. A “Christmas gift” for Lincoln. Confederate troops left Savannah, and Sherman’s army marched in without a battle. Thousands of freedom seekers had followed the army across Georgia. In January 1865 Sherman issued Field Order No. 15, setting aside coastal land for freed families.

clips.send: Atlanta. Its fall helped re-elect Lincoln. In July 1864 John Bell Hood replaced Johnston and attacked at Peachtree Creek (July 20) and the Battle of Atlanta (July 22). After Sherman cut the last railroad at Jonesboro, Hood left the city; Union troops entered on September 2, 1864. Sherman wired Washington: “Atlanta is ours, and fairly won.” The good news helped Lincoln win the November election. In November Sherman’s troops burned the city’s railroads, depots and factories before marching east.

clips.send: Andersonville. The deadliest prison camp of the war. Built in Sumter County, far from the fighting, to hold Union prisoners. About 45,000 men were held here; nearly 13,000 died, mostly of disease, poor food, bad water and exposure. The camp commander, Henry Wirz, was tried and executed after the war. Today it is home to the National Prisoner of War Museum, honoring all American POWs.

clips.send: Harpers Ferry. Today: Harpers Ferry, West Virginia. In October 1859 John Brown and 21 men seized the US arsenal here, hoping to arm enslaved people for an uprising. Marines captured him in the small brick fire-engine house now called “John Brown’s Fort”, which still stands where the Potomac and Shenandoah rivers meet.

clips.send: Chickamauga. The largest battle in Georgia. Confederate General Braxton Bragg attacked Union General William Rosecrans along Chickamauga Creek. A gap in the Union line let Confederates break through on September 20; General George Thomas held firm and became the “Rock of Chickamauga.” About 34,600 total casualties — second only to Gettysburg. A Confederate victory, but the Union kept Chattanooga, the gateway to Georgia.

clips.send: Kennesaw Mountain. Sherman’s one big frontal attack. Confederates dug in on the mountain. Sherman attacked head-on and lost about 3,000 men to about 1,000 Confederates. He went back to flanking moves, and Johnston retreated again. Nearby Big Shanty (today’s Kennesaw) is where Union raiders stole the locomotive “General” in the Great Locomotive Chase, April 1862.

clips.send: 安德森维尔。战争中死亡人数最多的战俘营。建在远离战场的萨姆特县，用来关押联邦战俘。 约 4.5 万人曾被关在这里；近 1.3 万人死亡，主要死于疾病、食物匮乏、脏水和日晒雨淋。 战俘营指挥官亨利·维尔茨战后受审并被处死。 今天这里是美国国家战俘博物馆，纪念所有美国战俘。

clips.send: 多尔顿与雷萨卡。亚特兰大战役开始。谢尔曼约 10 万大军在多尔顿附近对阵约瑟夫·E·约翰斯顿的约 6 万人。 谢尔曼不正面强攻，而是一次次迂回包抄约翰斯顿的侧翼，迫使他向南撤退。 双方都沿着西部与大西洋铁路行动——这是通往亚特兰大的生命线。

clips.send: 肯尼索山。谢尔曼唯一一次大规模正面进攻。邦联军在山上挖壕据守。谢尔曼正面强攻，损失约 3000 人，邦联约 1000 人。 他又回到迂回包抄的战术，约翰斯顿再次撤退。 附近的大棚屋（今肯尼索市）是 1862 年 4 月“火车头大追击”中联邦突击队偷走“将军号”机车的地方。

clips.send: 亚特兰大。它的陷落帮助林肯连任。1864 年 7 月，约翰·贝尔·胡德接替约翰斯顿，先后在桃树溪（7 月 20 日）和亚特兰大之战（7 月 22 日）发动进攻。 谢尔曼在琼斯伯勒切断最后一条铁路后，胡德撤出城市；9 月 2 日联邦军进城。 谢尔曼致电华盛顿：“亚特兰大是我们的了，赢得光明正大。”这个好消息帮助林肯赢得了 11 月的大选。 11 月，谢尔曼的部队在东进之前烧毁了城里的铁路、车站和工厂。

clips.send: 哈珀斯费里。今天：西弗吉尼亚州哈珀斯费里。1859年10月，约翰·布朗带领21人占领了这里的联邦军械库，想武装被奴役的人发动起义。海军陆战队在一座小砖房（消防车库）里抓住了他，这座房子今天叫“约翰·布朗堡”，仍然矗立在波托马克河与谢南多厄河的交汇处。

clips.send: 奇克莫加。佐治亚境内最大的战役。邦联将军布拉克斯顿·布拉格沿奇克莫加溪进攻联邦将军威廉·罗斯克兰斯。 9 月 20 日联邦防线出现缺口，邦联军突破；乔治·托马斯将军坚守阵地，被称为“奇克莫加的磐石”。 双方伤亡约 3.46 万人，仅次于葛底斯堡。邦联获胜，但联邦守住了通往佐治亚的门户查塔努加。
